result.title: RAGA: Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars from a Single Photo
result.summary: Avatars created from a single photo are fixed once made: regions the photo never showed, such as the back of a garment, are hallucinated and remain that way. We present Refreshable Animatable Gaussian Avatars (RAGA), a full-body Gaussian avatar that is created from a single image in about one second and can be refreshed whenever new images of the same person become available, without retraining or gradient-based optimization. RAGA maps each new observation into canonical UV space, accumulates it as visibility- and angle-weighted running sums, and re-decodes the fused map with the same decoder used for the photo. Although this decoder is trained only on single images, it makes use of the fused evidence. On 163 clips from five datasets, RAGA created from one photo outperforms LHM, LHM++ and IDOL, including on three datasets never used in training. Refreshing from later frames adds 0.49 dB PSNR overall and 0.68 dB on views turned at least 135° from the photo, where SSIM and LPIPS also improve. Given the same 16 images on all clips, LHM++ gains 0.15 dB, against 0.48 dB for RAGA. Creating an avatar takes 1.08 s and animating it 48.1 ms per frame on a laptop RTX 3080 GPU, with body fitting and matting included in creation and pose estimation included in animation. Code will be released on GitHub.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RAGA，从单张照片约 1 秒构建可动画的全身 Gaussian 头像，并在有新图像时把观测映射到规范化 UV 空间、按可见性与视角加权累加后重新解码，实现无需重训或梯度优化的「刷新」。
AI.relevance_reason: 其将多次观测以可见性和角度加权的 running sums 累积为可复用的规范化潜表示、再交由固定解码器使用，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与状态增量更新、以及训练分布外仍使用融合证据的问题。
